extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians and programmers working with polynomial/parametric systems)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage guidelines for procedures in the SINGULAR libraries (general.lib and grobcov.lib), describing purpose, usage signature, return value, options, notes, and examples for each procedure. Targets users who call these library routines to perform algebraic/computational tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: base2str
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library compregb.lib (see Section D.2.2.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced only by heading in this chunk; no detailed usage/return present in the extracted text.

rubrics_metrics.name: A_Z
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: A_Z("a",n); a any letter, n integer (-26<= n <=26, !=0). Return: string of n small (if a is small) or capital (if a is capital) letters, comma separated, beginning with a, in alphabetical order (or reverse alphabetical order if n<0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A_Z("c",5) -> "c,d,e,f,g"; A_Z("Z",-5) -> "Z,Y,X,W,V". Example of building a ring string: sR = "ring R = (0,"+A_Z("A",6)+"),("+A_Z("a",10)+"),dp;"; then execute(sR) to get coefficients comment and number of vars display.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ASCII([n,m]); n,m integers (32 <= n <= m <= 126). Returns a string of printable ASCII characters (no native language support). ASCII(): string of all ASCII characters with its numbers; ASCII(n): n-th ASCII character; ASCII(n,m): n-th up to m-th ASCII character (inclusive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text show ASCII() listing characters and codes, ASCII(42) -> '*', ASCII(32,126) -> full printable ASCII sequence. Demonstrates mapping between characters and numeric codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: absValue
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: absValue(c); c int, number or poly. Return: the absolute value of c; absValue(c)=c if c>=0; absValue=-c if c<=0. The function can be applied to any type for which comparison operators are defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: absValue(-2002) -> 2002; poly f=-4; absValue(f) -> 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: binomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: binomial(n,k); n,k integers. Return: binomial(n,k) (n choose k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: binomial(200,100) returns a bigint; compared against coeffs((x+1)^n,x)[k+1,1] to verify equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: deleteSublist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: deleteSublist(v,l); intvec v; list l where the entries of the integer vector v correspond to the positions of the elements to be deleted. Return: list without the deleted elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: list l=1,2,3,4,5; intvec v=1,3,4; l=deleteSublist(v,l); result -> list with remaining entries (2,5).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: factorial(n); n integer. Return: factorial(n): n! of type bigint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factorial(37) -> big integer value. See also reference to prime in section 5.1.115.

rubrics_metrics.name: fibonacci
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fibonacci(n); n,p integers. Return: fibonacci(n): nth Fibonacci number with f(0)=f(1)=1 and recurrence f(i+1)=f(i-1)+f(i), computed in characteristic 0, of type bigint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fibonacci(42) -> 267914296. (No further options shown.)

rubrics_metrics.name: kmemory
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: kmemory([n,[v]]); n,v integers. Return: memory in kilobyte of type bigint. n=0: memory used by active variables (same as no parameters). n=1: total memory allocated by Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If v!=0, display detailed information about allocated and used memory. Notes: kmemory uses internal function 'memory', and matches 'memory' for n!=0,1. Examples: kmemory() -> 149; kmemory(1,1) -> prints total memory allocated comment and returns numeric value.

rubrics_metrics.name: killall
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: killall(); killall("type name"); killall("not", "type name"); Return: kills user-defined variables per specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior: killall() kills all user-defined variables except loaded procedures. killall("type name") kills all user-defined variables of that type. killall("not","type name") kills all user-defined variables except those of the given type and except loaded procedures. killall("not","name1","name2",...) kills all user-defined variables except those named and except loaded procedures. Important note: 'killall' should never be used inside a procedure (it makes local variables global); examples show interactions with export/listvar and killing basering for level 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: number_e
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: number_e(n); n integer. Return: Euler number e=exp(1) up to n decimal digits (no rounding) - of type string if no basering of char 0 is defined - of type number if a basering of char 0 is defined. Display: decimal format of e if printlevel > 0 (default 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedure uses algorithm of A.H.J. Sale. Example: number_e(30) -> '2.71828182845904523536028747135'. Example also shows conversion to a rational approximation in a real basering.

rubrics_metrics.name: number_pi
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: number_pi(n); n positive integer. Return: pi (area of unit circle) up to n decimal digits (no rounding) - of type string if no basering of char 0 is defined - of type number if a basering of char 0 is defined. Display: decimal format of pi if printlevel > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: procedure uses algorithm of S. Rabinowitz. Example: number_pi(11) -> '3.1415926535'; in a real basering one gets a rounded numeric representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primes(n,m); n,m integers. Return: intvec consisting of all primes p with prime(n) <= p <= m in increasing order if n<=m, or in decreasing order if m<n. Note: prime(n) returns the biggest prime number <= min(n,32003) if n>=2, else 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: primes(50,100) -> 47,53,59,61,67,71,73,79,83,89,97. primes(37,1) -> descending list of primes starting at 37 down to 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: product
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: product(id[,v]); id ideal/vector/module/matrix/intvec/intmat/list, v intvec (default v=1..number of entries of id). The product of all entries of id (with index given by v). If id is not a list, it is treated as list of polys or integers. A module is identified with corresponding matrix. If v is outside range, empty product returns 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: product(maxideal(1)) -> xyz; product(M) for a matrix multiplies all entries appropriately; product on intvec subsets returns integer product; product on intmat returns product of selected entries. Behavior depends on input types (ideal/module/list/etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: sort
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sort(id[,v,o,n]); id = ideal/module/intvec/list. sort may be called with 1, 2 or 3 arguments. Returns a list l of two elements: l[1] object of same type as input but sorted; l[2] intvec describing the permutation. Sorting rules differ by input type: ideals/modules sorted w.r.t. intvec v (or ordering o or actual monomial ordering), lists/intvec sorted w.r.t. <. Note: generators with SMALLER leading term come FIRST (sort(id) sorts backwards to actual monomial ordering). If n!=0 ordering is inverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: n=0. If 'o' is given input is sorted by considering leading terms w.r.t. new ring ordering. Zero generators of ideal/module are deleted. Examples show sort(i), sort(i,3..1), sort(i,"ls")[1]. Notes/warnings: for integer vectors or lists with negative integers, behavior may be buggy; do not use sort for integer vectors or lists with potential negative integers. Also shows how to sort modules w.r.t. new ordering by considering old leading terms (several equivalent commands).

rubrics_metrics.name: sum
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sum(id[,v]); id ideal/vector/module/matrix/intvec/intmat/list, v intvec (default v=1..number of entries). The sum of all entries of id (with index given by v). If id not a list treat as list of polys/integers. If v outside range empty sum returns 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sum of vector pv returns polynomial sum; sum of matrix columns returns sum of selected entries; sum over intvec gives integer sum; sum over sequence x(3..7), intvec picks elements by indices. Example: sum(intvec(1..100)) -> 5050.

rubrics_metrics.name: watchdog
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: watchdog(i, cmd) where result of cmd is returned if the result can be computed in i seconds; otherwise computation is interrupted after i seconds, string "Killed" is returned and global variable 'watchdog interrupt' is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: current basering should not be watchdog rneu since watchdog rneu will be killed. If variables named by structure x(i) exist, polynomials must be put into eval(...) for correct interpretation. A second Singular process is started by this procedure. Example: watchdog(1,"sleep(5)") -> Killed; watchdog(10,"sleep(5)") -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: primecoeffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primecoeffs(J[,p]); J any type convertible to a matrix (vector, module, int, intvec), p integer. Compute prime factors <= p of coefficients of J (default p = 32003). Return: a list l of two intvectors: l[1] different prime factors of all coefficients of J; l[2] different remaining factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: primecoeffs(intvec(7*8*121,7*8)) -> shows prime factors; primecoeffs on an ideal shows partitions of coefficient factors into small primes and remnant factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: timeStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: timeStd(i,d), i ideal, d integer. Return: std(i) if the standard basis computation finished after d-1 seconds and i otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows using timeStd to run standard basis computation with time cutoff and inspecting which result was returned depending on time taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: timeFactorize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: timeFactorize(p,d); poly p, integer d. Return: factorize(p) if the factorization finished after d-1 seconds otherwise f is considered to be irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example illustrates wrapping factorization in a time limit to avoid long computations; used in examples with p^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: factorH(p) p poly. Return: factorize(p). Note: changes variables to make the last variable the principal one in multivariate factorization and then factorizes the polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to improve factorization behavior by reordering variables. Example: factorH used on a polynomial where direct factorize behavior differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: grobcov.lib (library overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: grobcov.lib. Purpose: Groebner Cover for parametric ideals. Contains Montes-Wibmer algorithms for computing the Canonical Groebner Cover of a parametric ideal. Central routine is grobcov. The library includes many related routines (ConsLevels, locus, locusdg, locusto, envelop) and utilities for dynamic geometry and automatic deduction of geometric theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview discusses theoretical background, references (papers, book), authors, and applications (parametric polynomial systems, Comprehensive Groebner Systems, Canonical Forms, loci, envelopes, dynamic geometry). Notations: before calling routines user must define ideal Q[a][x] and input polynomials on it; internally routines define other ideals like Q[a], Q[x,a].

rubrics_metrics.name: grobcov (procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: grobcov(ideal F[,options]); F: ideal in Q[a][x] (a=parameters, x=variables) to be discussed. Return: the Groebner Cover of a parametric ideal F, a list [[lpp1,basis1,segment1],...,[lpps,basiss,segments]] optionally with homogenized lpph. The lpp are constant over a segment and correspond to the set of lpp of the reduced Groebner basis for each point of the segment. Basis entries are I-regular functions given in full representation (option "ext",1) or generic representation (default "ext",0). Segment representations can be P-representation (default) or C-representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed options (pairs string,integer): "null",ideal E (default ideal(0)) and "nonnull",ideal N (default ideal(1)) restrict parameter space to V(E) \ V(N). "can",0-1 (default 1) determines whether homogenized ideal is computed for canonical Groebner Cover; setting 0 shortens computation but result not exactly canonical. "ext",0-1 (default 0) controls full vs generic representation of bases (full may yield simpler result but more time). "rep",0-1-2 (default 0) selects P-representation (canonical), C-representation, or both. "comment",0-3 (default 0) increases computation commentary. "showhom",0-1 (default 0) includes lpp of homogenized ideal as informational string. P-representation form: [[p1,[p11,..]],...], representing union of V(p_i) \ union V(p_ij) where p's are prime ideals. C-representation: (E,N) representing V(E) \ V(N) with E,N radical and N contains E. Example calls and illustrative computations (Casas conjecture, robotics examples) are provided showing ring setup, ideal definitions, and grobcov(F) output structure.
